sentences.text:
Neutral Citation No. - 2024:Ahc:132352
Court No. - 71
Case :- Criminal Revision No. - 3189 of 2024

Revisionist :- Mr X- Juvenile
Opposite Party :- State Of U.P. And 3 Others
Counsel for Revisionist :- Nazia Nafees

Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Mayank Kumar Jain,J.
1.
Heard Ms. Nazia Nafees, learned counsel for revisionist, learned AGA for the State and perused the record.

2. This criminal revision under Section 102 of Juvenile Justice (Care & Protection of Children) Act,
2015 has been filed against order dated 3.5.2024 passed by Mahendra Kumar-II Child Court/Special Court Additional Session Judge/Special Judge Pocso Act, Fatehpur in Criminal Appeal No. 28 of 2024 as well as the impugned order dated 1.2.2024 passed by learned Juvenile Justice Board,
Fatehpur in Case Crime No. 233 of 2023 under Sections 363, 366, 376 I.P.C. P.S. Lalauli, District Fatehpur, whereby a revisionist has been denied bail.

entities.text:
Juvenile Justice (Care & Protection of Children) Act,
2015
entities.label: STATUTE

entities.text: Child Court/Special Court Additional Session Judge/Special Judge Pocso Act, Fatehpur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: It is also prayed to release the revisionist during trial of the present criminal revision.
3. It is submitted by learned counsel for the applicant that revisionist is innocent and he has been falsely implicated in the present case.
There are material contradictions in the statement of prosecutrix recorded under Sections 161 and 164 Cr.P.C.
The DNA report is still awaited.
The prosecutrix was found to be pregnant.

It is further submitted that at the time of incident, the Mr X- Juvenile vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 14 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/142196225/
1 prosecutrix was major, while revisionist was minor.

entities.text: Mr X- Juvenile vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Being major, she appears to be a consenting party.

It is further submitted that during her statement recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C., the prosecutrix stated that the revisionist induced her and had taken her to Fatehpur, while during her statement recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C., she made allegation against the revisionist that along with two other persons, revisionist induced her and had taken her to Pune.
It is also submitted that the report of District Probation Officer is not adverse to the applicant.
Lastly, it is submitted that applicant is in observation since 13.10.2023.
4. Per contra, learned A.G.A. has opposed the revision and submitted that the revisionist has committed serious offence.
However, he could not dispute the submissions urged by learned counsel for revisionist as well as facts noted above.

5. Having heard learned counsel for revisionist, learned AGA for the State, learned counsel for the informant and upon perusal of the statements of prosecutrix, this Court finds that prosecutrix did not support the version of the FIR, then there is no reason to detain the revisionist.

Consequently,
the present revision is liable to be allowed.
6. Accordingly, the present criminal revision succeeds and is hereby allowed.
Impugned order dated 3.5.2024 is hereby quashed.

7. Let the revisionist-applicant, named above, be released on bail in this case on furnishing an undertaking by guardian/father that he will take proper care over the revisionist-applicant and he will not allow him to go in the company of known criminals or expose him to moral, physical or psychological danger and he will also file a personal bond of Rs.50,000/- and two sureties of the like amount to the satisfaction of Magistrate concerned.
Order Date :- 14.8.2024 SY  Mr X- Juvenile vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 14 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/142196225/
